# Define the URL of the Python module to be downloaded from Dropbox.
# The 'dl=1' parameter in the URL forces a direct download of the file content.
url= 'https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/4y5hjxlfphh1ngvbgo77q/\
module_-basic_concepts_fixed_income.py?rlkey=6oxi7mgka42veaat79hcv8boz&st=87sztshr&dl=1'
module_name='basic_concepts_fixed_income'
# Send an HTTP GET request to the URL and store the server's response.
try:
    response = requests.get(url)
    module = ModuleType(module_name)
    exec(response.text, module.__dict__)
    sys.modules[module_name] = module
    
    # Now we can import from our in-memory module
    from basic_concepts_fixed_income import (secure_key_setup)
    FredReader=module.FredReader
except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
    print(f"❌ Error: Could not fetch module from URL. {e}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"❌ Error: Failed to execute or import the module. {e}")

🚀 secure_key_setup makes the FRED API available to the notebook

children.label: 🚀 secure_key_setup makes the FRED API available to the notebook

children.value: This function is a smart setup wizard that safely loads your FRED API key into the notebook environment.
Seamless Loading: If you have already saved your key in a previous session, it automatically finds it and loads it into the background.
Secure Storage: If your key is missing, it launches an interactive UI to help you safely vault your key (using Google Colab Secrets or hidden local files) so you never accidentally share it.
Live Validation: Before loading, it actively pings the FRED servers to ensure your key is valid and active, instantly catching typos or formatting errors.
Cross-Environment: It automatically detects if you are running on Google Colab, a local Jupyter server, or a temporary Binder session, and adapts its security protocols accordingly.
